spec.description: Edogawa, Tokyo, building by building: PLATEAU's 3D city model (CityGML) of the ward's 144,788 buildings, each coloured by the water PLATEAU's river and storm surge studies expect there, with linked charts of depth, days under water, storeys and use that filter the map in the browser, and the shelters.

options.content:
### What this shows

Edogawa is the easternmost of Tokyo's 23 wards, home to about 680,000 people between the Arakawa, the Nakagawa,
the Edogawa and Tokyo Bay. Much of it lies below sea level, sunk by groundwater pumping in the last century, and
held dry by levees and sea walls. If the Tone or the Edogawa broke through in the worst rain thought possible,
or the largest typhoon assumed pushed Tokyo Bay over the walls, almost every building in the ward would stand in
water, in many places for two weeks or more. The ward's own hazard map says it plainly: in such a flood, leave
the ward.

The map draws each of PLATEAU's 144,788 buildings as the city model has it and colours it by the deepest water
the study picked expects there. The charts beside it are of the same buildings, held in your browser: drag across
one, or click a use, and the map, the figures and the other charts keep only those buildings.

### Where the data comes from

- **[PLATEAU](https://www.mlit.go.jp/plateau/)**, Japan's 3D city models by the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure,
  Transport and Tourism: [Edogawa-ku, FY2023](https://www.geospatial.jp/ckan/dataset/plateau-13123-edogawa-ku-2023),
  CityGML v4 (free for any use with credit, compatible with CC BY 4.0). Each building carries the flood studies
  that reach it: the national and Tokyo governments' river studies (depth, band and, for the largest assumed
  floods, how long water of 0.5 m or more stays) and Tokyo's storm surge study of March 2018 (depth and band).
  The shelters are PLATEAU's related data.
- **[Flateau](https://source.coop/pacificspatial/flateau)** by Pacific Spatial Solutions (CC BY 4.0): PLATEAU's
  attributes as tables, with the same building ids. The 3D files (converted with citygml-tools) carry the
  geometry; Flateau the attributes, which citygml-tools leaves out.

### How to read it

- **Study.** Largest river flood (L2): the worst rain thought possible, about once in 1,000 years, for every
  river PLATEAU has. Planned river flood (L1): the flood the river works are designed for, about once in 200
  years, studied only for the Tone and the Edogawa: their water comes from the north and stops at the
  Shin-Nakagawa, the canal across the ward, so the south-west stays grey. Storm surge: Tokyo Bay.
- **Source.** Each river study floods the ward from one river's broken levee. "Any" takes the worst of them at
  each building, which no single flood would do at once.
- **Colours** are PLATEAU's depth bands, those of Japan's hazard maps: under 0.5 m, 0.5 to 3 m (the ground
  floor), 3 to 5 m (the first floor up), 5 m or more; grey, no water there in that study, or left out by a brush.
- **Storeys** are PLATEAU's (106,142 buildings have them); "no floor above the water" assumes 3 m a floor.
- Not in these studies: the Arakawa, the largest river on the ward's west side.
- Most buildings are drawn as blocks of their measured height (LoD 1); PLATEAU has detailed roofs (LoD 2) for
  3,990. On another Pacha, set the hidden variable `site` to its https address: the 3D files are served there.

spec.rawSql:
-- Buildings by PLATEAU's depth band in each study (the deepest of its rivers), side by side.
WITH b AS (
  SELECT key, scenario, max(band) AS band FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/edogawa-flood/flood.parquet' GROUP BY key, scenario
)
SELECT ['under 0.5 m', '0.5 to 3 m', '3 to 5 m', '5 m or more'][band] AS "Water",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE scenario = 'L1') AS "River, planned scale (L1)",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE scenario = 'L2') AS "River, largest assumed (L2)",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE scenario = 'Surge') AS "Storm surge"
FROM b GROUP BY band ORDER BY band

spec.description: Buildings by PLATEAU's depth band in each study, any river. The planned scale (L1) is the flood the river works are designed for, studied only for the Tone and the Edogawa (about once in 200 years); the largest assumed (L2) is the worst rain thought possible (about once in 1,000 years), for every river PLATEAU has; the storm surge is Tokyo's 2018 study of the largest typhoon assumed over Tokyo Bay.
spec.title: The three studies side by side

spec.description: Buildings by the days water of 0.5 m or more stays round them. PLATEAU has a duration only for the largest assumed river floods (L2), and not for every river: empty for the planned scale and the storm surge.
spec.title: How long the water stays

spec.rawSql:
-- The tiles (box and CityJSON), then one row per building under water that the brushes keep:
-- the City Model layer colours those by key and leaves the others grey.
SELECT city_url, west, south, east, north, NULL::DOUBLE AS key, NULL::DOUBLE AS depth_m FROM $tiles
UNION ALL
SELECT NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, key, depth_m FROM $bld WHERE $__crossfilter($bldFilters)
SELECT name, kind, height_m, water_l2_m, latitude, longitude FROM $shelters

spec.description: PLATEAU's 3D model of Edogawa (CityGML: each building's block, and its LoD 2 model where PLATEAU has one), coloured by the deepest water the study picked expects at it, in PLATEAU's depth bands. Grey: no water there in that study, or left out by the charts' brushes. Hover a building for its storeys, use and the water in every study; white dots are the ward's shelters. The 1 km tiles load as the view moves.
spec.title: Every building of Edogawa, by the water PLATEAU expects there

spec.rawSql:
-- The ward's shelters, the deepest water round them first (largest assumed river flood, any river).
SELECT name AS "Shelter", height_m AS "Height (m)", water_l2_m AS "Water (m)",
       floor((height_m - coalesce(water_l2_m, 0)) / 3)::INTEGER AS "Dry floors"
FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/edogawa-flood/shelters.parquet'
ORDER BY water_l2_m DESC NULLS LAST, name

spec.description: The ward's 163 designated shelters (PLATEAU's related data; names as the ward gives them), the height of the building and the deepest water PLATEAU expects at the buildings within 30 m in the largest assumed river flood (any river). Dry floors: the building's height over the water, 3 m a floor.
spec.title: Shelters

spec.rawSql:
SELECT count(*)::DOUBLE AS "Buildings under water",
       100.0 * count(*) / (SELECT sum(buildings) FROM $tiles) AS "Of the ward",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE depth_m >= 3)::DOUBLE AS "3 m or more",
       sum(no_dry_floor)::DOUBLE AS "No floor above the water",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE days >= 14)::DOUBLE AS "Two weeks or more"
FROM $bld WHERE $__crossfilter($bldFilters)

spec.description: Of PLATEAU's 144,788 buildings in Edogawa, those under water in the study picked and kept by the charts' brushes: with 3 m or more (the ground floor under), with no floor above the water (storeys times 3 m, for the 106,142 buildings whose storeys PLATEAU gives) and with water of 0.5 m or more for two weeks or longer (PLATEAU has how long the water stays only for the largest assumed river floods).
spec.title: The ward under water

spec.description: Buildings under water by their storeys above ground (PLATEAU gives them for 106,142 of the ward's buildings; those over 15 storeys are off the right edge). Most are houses of two storeys: 3 m of water fills the ground floor, 6 m the whole house.
spec.title: How tall

spec.rawSql:
SELECT usage AS "Use", count(*)::DOUBLE AS "Wet",
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE depth_m >= 3)::DOUBLE AS "3 m +",
       sum(no_dry_floor)::DOUBLE AS "No dry floor",
       median(storeys) AS "Storeys"
FROM $bld WHERE $__crossfilter($bldFilters)
GROUP BY usage ORDER BY count(*) DESC

query.rawSql:
-- Server side, once per scenario and source: one row per building PLATEAU's study puts under
-- water (the deepest of the rivers picked), with what the building is. The browser holds it
-- and every brush is answered there.
WITH w AS (
  SELECT key, max(depth_m) AS depth_m, max(band) AS band, max(hours) AS hours
  FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/edogawa-flood/flood.parquet'
  WHERE scenario = ${scenario:sqlstring}
    AND (${river:sqlstring} = 'any' OR river = ${river:sqlstring})
  GROUP BY key
)
SELECT w.key, w.depth_m,
       ['under 0.5 m', '0.5 to 3 m', '3 to 5 m', '5 m or more'][w.band] AS band,
       w.hours / 24 AS days, b.storeys, b.height_m, b.usage,
       (w.depth_m >= 3 * b.storeys)::INTEGER AS no_dry_floor
FROM w JOIN 'http://feeds/datasets/edogawa-flood/buildings.parquet' b USING (key)

-- Server side, once per visit: PLATEAU's 1 km tiles of buildings, each box and its CityJSON on
-- this site (the City Model layer fetches it from the viewer's browser: an https address).
SELECT ${site:sqlstring} || '/datasets/edogawa-flood/cityjson/m' || mesh || '.json' AS city_url,
       west, south, east, north, buildings
FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/edogawa-flood/tiles.parquet'

-- Server side, once per visit: the ward's shelters (PLATEAU's related data), with the deepest
-- water PLATEAU expects at the buildings within 30 m of each in the largest assumed river flood.
SELECT name, kind, height_m, water_l2_m, lat AS latitude, lon AS longitude
FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/edogawa-flood/shelters.parquet'

-- Server side, once per visit: the ward's border.
SELECT wkt FROM 'http://feeds/datasets/edogawa-flood/border.parquet'
